title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (July 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET — FOMC day one, as every July print is
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-07-27 is the last Tuesday of July 2027. The rule is verified for JULY specifically, 3 of 3 and every one of the three DOUBLE-SOURCED, against the publisher's own pages fetched direct 2026-09-06 and each read against its own "Source: July <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line rather than trusted by slug: CCI-July-2022 (644,517 bytes, released 2022-07-26), CCI-July-2023 (1,528,271 bytes, 2023-07-25) and CCI-July-2024 (1,015,724 bytes, 2024-07-30) -- each the last Tuesday of its July, and each independently named IN ADVANCE by the preceding June edition's own next-release line, re-fetched this session: CCI-June-2022 "The next release is Tuesday, July 26 at 10 AM ET", CCI-June-2023 "Tuesday, July 25", CCI-June-2024 "Tuesday, July 30th". CCI-July-2021, CCI-July-2025 and CCI-July-2026 each returned HTTP 200 while serving the current August 2026 edition (332,006 bytes) and are recorded as blocked rather than counted. No July-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a three-deep double-sourced July record rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the consumer-confidence-2027-07-27 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-07-27.from-consumer-confidence-2027-06-29.json, which is now inert. THAT PROPOSAL'S HEADLINE CLAIM IS REFUTED, and the replacement is deterministic. It filed this id as an FOMC day-one collision that "gives 2027 TWO collisions from one release rule, which no year in the 2021-2026 tape has." Parsed off the Fed's own posted calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes; 56 meetings, and the 8-meetings-per-year assertion the 06-29 sibling banked was asserted and held), 2027 has FOUR collisions -- 01-26, 04-27, 07-27, 10-26 -- and EVERY year in the record has two to four (2021:3, 2022:2, 2023:3, 2024:3, 2025:3, 2026:4, 2027:4). The mechanism is mechanical, not annual: EVERY FOMC day one falling in January, April, July or October IS the last Tuesday of that month, 22 of 22, gap zero every time, while the SEP meetings (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) sit 7 to 21 days earlier and can never collide (0 of 28). A collision is a property of WHICH MONTH the Fed's non-SEP meeting lands in, and 2027 is unremarkable. THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS FOR THIS EVENT: July has never once printed clean -- 0 of 6 -- so the chain's 51-day CLEAN-CB-DAY null, the baseline every sibling stance in this series rests on, contains ZERO July observations (and zero January ones) and cannot speak to this print at all. The right comparison set is the colliding one, and July is null there too: vs other FOMC day-ones 0 of 9 (n=6 vs 39, smallest p QQQ 0.1872), vs other July 0 of 9, vs other late-July 0 of 9, vs all sessions 0 of 9. JULY'S CUT-OFF LAGS, the gap the 06-29 sibling named as unmeasured, are now sourced at 5/6/8 days (2022-07-21, 2023-07-19, 2024-07-22) -- the 5-day lag is the shortest anywhere in the chain and the 5-to-8 spread the widest within any single month, which refines the sibling's rule: the lag varies WITHIN a month too, so project a range (2027 cut-off 07-19 to 07-22, field window 07-04/07 -> 07-19/22) and never a point. THAT WINDOW IS THE CHAIN'S CLEANEST TRANSMISSION SITE AND ALWAYS HAS BEEN: a July panel is 100% post-SEP-decision AND closes before the July FOMC convenes, 7 of 7, so the 06-29 sibling's 76% is not the sharpest site in the record -- every July beats it -- and the test already runs on the three sourced July editions, holding 3 of 3 (no edition attributes its month-over-month move to an FOMC decision; CCI-July-2023 says its move came "Despite rising interest rates"). AND THE CHAIN'S 80-THRESHOLD PREMISE IS REFUTED BY THE SAME FETCH: CCI-July-2023 prints Expectations at 88.3 -- "Expectations climbed well above 80" -- one month after the June 2023 reading the sibling called the closest approach any sourced edition had made, and that crossing was a FALSE recession signal (the Board still wrote "we still anticipate one likely before yearend"). CCI-July-2023 also restates June 2023's Expectations at exactly 80.0, up from its 79.3 first print. CORRIDOR: zero tracked events exist anywhere in July or August 2027 today; three are proposed in this PR, of which fomc-2027-07-28 is the FOMC decision one session after this print -- the day the measured Fed effect actually lives (decision days 8 of 9 wider, SPY 1.352/0.958 p=0.0001; day ones 0 of 9). Estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
